title: Annual moment sums showed no clear concentration excess under regional shuffles in Global CMT Mw 5.8+ data for 1982-2020
abstract: We tested whether annual sums of seismic moment had excess concentration after event times and regional counts were fixed. We used 7,580 Global CMT earthquakes with Mw at least 5.8 in 1982-2020. We exchanged scalar moments within 20-degree cells, three depth groups, and two method eras. The annual concentration was 0.07398. Its exact shuffle mean was 0.08845, and the central 95% shuffle range was 0.07418-0.12790. The upper-tail Monte Carlo p value was 0.9787 from 19,999 draws. An exact decomposition assigned 74.3% of observed concentration to individual event terms that cannot change when event years are exchanged. Global exchange, finer cells, other magnitude cuts, July-June years and three-year bins also gave no upper-tail excess. A small lower-tail departure in the primary test did not hold under other bin choices. This is a conditional test of moment allocation, not a test of constant global hazard. Few very large events, uncertain moments, catalog changes and exchange assumptions limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, all test-statistic draws, source hashes and independent arithmetic checks support reproduction. External event records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Annual moment shares, the primary shuffle distribution, the exact self and distinct-event decomposition, and five exchange rules. Horizontal ranges are central 95% shuffle ranges, not confidence intervals for physical rates. The primary observed statistic lies below its central range. No tested rule shows an upper-tail excess.
